newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat strong near-term, down in later months.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat strong near-term, down in later months.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures stayed strong in near-term months but fell to more realistic levels in later months in a moderately active market on Thursday.
In traded contracts, September 1997 rose by A$1.00 a tonne to A$200.00 on 16 lots, but November 1997 and January 1998 fell, by A$3.50 and A$8.00 respectively, to both end at A$177.00.
Across the range, settlement prices rose by A$1.00-A$1.50 for near-term May, July and September 1997 but fell, mostly by about A$8.00, in the more distant contracts.
Garry Hopper of ANZ Futures Ltd said the market reflected dry conditions with buyers prepared to pay for short-term wheat. This showed in near September 1997's rise to A$200.00.
November 1997, at a settlement price of A$179.00, was heavily discounted against September 1997 at its settlement of A$200.50, he pointed out.
January, with the contract for that month on a settlement price of A$176.50, was where the new crop wheat would start coming into play, he said.
"In the short-term we're just seeing a bit of a squeeze in the cash market," he said.
Chris Gray of C A & L Bell Commodities Corp said Thursday's market settled into a more realistic pattern after Wednesday's close.
September 1997 was surprisingly strong but the back months were pretty much fair value, he said.
The market would be looking for rain over the next two weeks and, if it received it, was likely to follow the U.S. in the downward trend it had shown over the past two weeks, he said.
